items.title: 56800_John Simmons oral history interview
items.q: And they had a comedian there named Willy Lewis. He was funny, but he was funnier offstage than he was onstage.

ctx.x: By that you mean a main showroom?

Yes. Dinah Washington was the headliner. And they had a comedian there named Willy Lewis. He was funny, but he was funnier offstage than he was onstage. He had a little skit, he'd come out of the audience, you know, and he twirled the baton, that was part of his act. He didn't dance. Just twirling the baton and talking, you know, and he was telling this joke about this fellow that was going to train this flea to talk. So he put this flea in a penny matchbox -- a penny. You can't get that anymore. He had this flea…

for his bed and everything, and every morning he would open the box and say, 'Good morning, little flea.' Trying to get him to talk. So finally, one morning, the flea said, 'Good morning.' He said, 'Oh, I've got it. I've got the greatest act in the world.' So he took him to an agent and said, 'I've got an act.' The agent said, 'What kind of an act do you have?' He said, 'I've got a flea.' He said, 'Oh, man, we've got millions of flea acts.' He said, 'No, not like this one. This one talks.' He said, 'If you don't…
